Three Kuki men were killed in a fresh exchange of gunfire between unidentified armed groups in Manipur’s Noney district on Saturday, even as thousands of people, including members of Meitei and Naga organisations, held a rally in Imphal demanding the scrapping of the Suspension of Operations (SoO) agreement with Kuki-Zo armed groups and greater protection for local communities. The firing took place around 10am at Kekru Naga village under Nungba police station, officials aware of the matter said.
news.full_article_text: 3 Kukis shot dead in Manipur gunfight Three Kuki men were killed in Manipur gunfire as Meitei and Naga groups rallied in Imphal to scrap the SoO pact with Kuki-Zo armed groups. Three Kuki men were killed in a fresh exchange of gunfire between unidentified armed groups in Manipur’s Noney district on Saturday, even as thousands of people, including members of Meitei and Naga organisations, held a rally in Imphal demanding the scrapping of the Suspension of Operations (SoO) agreement with Kuki-Zo armed groups and greater protection for local communities. The firing took place around 10am at Kekru Naga village under Nungba police station, officials aware of the matter said. Sporadic gunfire between unidentified groups suspected to belong to the Naga and Kuki communities had been reported in the area since October 29, said police, adding that Saturday’s incident was the first in three days to result in fatalities. According to police, security forces have been deployed in the area to maintain law and order. The three men have been identified as Thanglensang Singson, Thangkhosei Haokip and Lamminsang Kipgen, all residents of villages in Churachandpur district, police said. Kuki Inpi Manipur (KIM), a Kuki apex body, accused the National Socialist Council of Nagaland-Isak Muivah (NSCN-IM) and the Zeliangrong United Front-Kamson (ZUF-K) of responsibility for the killings. It said the three men were village volunteers. “The murder of these three brave village volunteers in Noney district is the direct consequence of the state’s reckless refusal to provide adequate security to vulnerable Kuki-Zo communities,” the organisation said in a statement. According to police, four automatic assault rifles, a single-barrel rifle, a drone, ammunition and improvised explosives were recovered from the site. Meanwhile, a massive rally, jointly organised by the Meitei and Naga communities, swept through Imphal on Saturday in what was arguably one of the largest public gatherings in Manipur since ethnic violence erupted in 2023. The high-turnout demonstration comes on the heels of a recent flare-up in tensions involving both groups and the Kuki-Zo community. They demanded the termination of the SoO agreement with Kuki-Zo armed groups and rehabilitation of families displaced by the ethnic conflict. The rally was jointly organised by the Coordinating Committee on Manipur Integrity (COCOMI), United Naga Council (UNC), Joint Tribes Council (JTC), Foot Hills Naga Coordinating Committee (FNCC), Naga People Union, Imphal (NPUI), Naga Humanitarian Aid Committee Manipur (NHACM), Manipur Naga Youth Organisation (MNYO), All Naga Students’ Association, Manipur (ANSAM), and people from the hills and valley. It came days after militants ambushed 14 Meitei men, killing three of them, sparking protests in the state. The conflict between Meitei and Kuki communities has claimed at least 306 lives so far, while clashes between Kuki and Naga groups have killed around 50 people since February. Officials said the march began at Tiddim Ground and concluded at Thangmeiband Athletic Union (THAU) ground in Imphal West. Police put up barricades at Keisampat junction, near Lok Bhavan, the chief minister’s office and the BJP state office, preventing the procession from moving further. No untoward incident was reported, said a senior police officer. At a public convention held at THAU ground, participants adopted a six-point resolution demanding an immediate end to what they described as the Centre’s “proxy war” and its support for “narco-terrorism”. They also sought the deployment of a neutral security force along the India-Myanmar border. The convention demanded that the SoO arrangement, which expired on September 24, not be extended under any circumstances. It called for the dismantling of designated camps, seizure of weapons and action against cadres accused of violating the agreement’s ground rules. The organisations also demanded permanent rehabilitation of internally displaced people (IDPs) since May 3, 2023, with adequate security, restoration of properties and livelihood support to enable their return. Another resolution sought the replacement of the Assam Rifles along the India-Myanmar border with a neutral, professionally trained force to prevent infiltration, trafficking and other cross-border crimes. The groups also demanded implementation of the National Register of Citizens (NRC), with 1951 as the base year, and the removal of deputy chief minister Nemcha Kipgen from the cabinet. They called for the government’s resignation if she was not removed. Naga organisations have accused Kipgen’s husband, Thangboi Kipgen, chairman of the Kuki National Front-Presidential faction, of involvement in civilian killings. Deputy chief minister Losii Dikho has also made the allegation. “Today, after three and a half years of crisis in Manipur, the indigenous people of the state, particularly the 21-22 tribes of the Nagas, the Meitei communities and several other ethnic groups, have come together to raise their voice against the government of India,” said Khuraijam Athouba, a former COCOMI convener. Athouba accused the Centre of failing to protect lives and property and said the agitation would continue until the demands were addressed. The Committee on Tribal Unity (CoTU) also held a parallel rally in Kangpokpi, citing threats to civilian lives and continued injustice against the Kuki-Zo community. It extended a total shutdown across the district by another 24 hours, citing the failure to secure the safe recovery of two missing Kuki civilians. It had earlier advised Kuki-Zo people against travelling beyond Kuki-inhabited areas of Sadar Hills. At a National Unity Day event in Imphal, chief minister Y Khemchand Singh said community-centric thinking could not ensure peace or economic progress. “A state cannot be governed by prioritising the interest of only one community,” he said.

news.story_lead: Jaishankar meets Russian FM Lavrov in Atlanta, discusses Ukraine, West Asia situation Jaishankar meets Lavrov in Atlanta to discuss Ukraine, Gulf tensions and global issues. External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar met Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov in Atlanta, where the two discussed the Ukraine conflict, the situation in the Gulf and wider international issues. The meeting took place on the sidelines of the G20 Foreign Ministers’ Meeting, hosted by US Secretary of State Marco Rubio on October 30 and 31.

External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar met Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov in Atlanta, where the two discussed the Ukraine conflict, the situation in the Gulf and wider international issues. The meeting took place on the sidelines of the G20 Foreign Ministers’ Meeting, hosted by US Secretary of State Marco Rubio on October 30 and 31. Jaishankar shared a photograph with Lavrov on X on Saturday, October 31, confirming the meeting. “Discussed the Ukraine conflict, Gulf situation and multilateral issues with FM Sergey Lavrov of Russia,” he wrote. The meeting comes as the Russia-Ukraine war continues to divide world leaders and tensions in West Asia raise concerns over energy supplies, shipping routes and regional security. Jaishankar, Lavrov discuss Ukraine and Gulf tensions Deep Dive The two foreign ministers discussed the ongoing Ukraine conflict, the Gulf situation and multilateral issues. India has continued to engage with Russia through high-level diplomatic meetings despite differences between Moscow and Western countries over the war in Ukraine. India has also maintained its position that dialogue and diplomacy are important for resolving international conflicts. Jaishankar also called for diplomacy over military action while addressing the G20 gathering. He said military solutions would not work in dealing with global challenges and stressed that diplomacy should be given a chance. The two-day gathering in Atlanta was hosted by US Secretary of State Marco Rubio. Russia's participation also became a point of tension, with several European representatives objecting to appearing alongside Lavrov in the traditional group photograph. Rubio eventually cancelled the group photo. The meeting ended without a joint communique as members failed to reach an agreement on several major issues. Instead, the United States planned to issue a chairman's statement outlining the discussions. news.story_lead: Supreme Court registers suo motu contempt case over Kerala Congress' derogatory post against CJI Surya Kant Converting separate letters addressed by two lawyers into a common petition on Friday, the court has tentatively listed the matter on November 6. The Supreme Court has registered a suo motu writ petition seeking contempt of court action against Kerala Pradesh Congress Committee (KPCC) for publishing a derogatory post against Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant. Converting separate letters addressed by two lawyers – Vineet Jindal and Sreejesh SR – into a common petition on Friday, the registry of the Supreme Court has tentatively listed the matter to November 6.
news.full_article_text: Supreme Court registers suo motu contempt case over Kerala Congress' derogatory post against CJI Surya Kant Converting separate letters addressed by two lawyers into a common petition on Friday, the court has tentatively listed the matter on November 6. The Supreme Court has registered a suo motu writ petition seeking contempt of court action against Kerala Pradesh Congress Committee (KPCC) for publishing a derogatory post against Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant. Converting separate letters addressed by two lawyers – Vineet Jindal and Sreejesh SR – into a common petition on Friday, the registry of the Supreme Court has tentatively listed the matter to November 6. Track live updates on anti-SIR protest Jindal wrote a letter to the CJI on October 13 citing a post published by KPCC on ‘X’ that was subsequently deleted. The post published addressed the CJI as “Dear Surya Kant” and stated, “If law and order is not your domain, resign now. We will find your replacement who can handle it.” The post that kicked up a row was published on October 12 amid the hearing by the top court on a bunch of petitions seeking probe into excesses by the Delhi Police during the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) protests in the capital city. Also read: Kharge accuses CEC Gyanesh Kumar of 'treason', levels 6 charges during INDIA bloc's mock impeachment Following the controversial post, the two bar associations of the Supreme Court – Supreme Court Bar Association (SCBA) and Supreme Court Advocates on Record Association (SCOARA) – condemned the demand for CJI’s resignation. news.headline: ISRO Successfully Launches NVS-03 Satellite to Enhance India's NavIC Navigation Network
news.story_lead: The Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) has successfully launched the NVS-03 satellite into orbit. This mission provides a strategic boost to NavIC (Navigation with Indian Constellation), strengthening India's self-reliant positioning and navigation infrastructure.
news.full_article_text:
### ISRO Launches NVS-03 Satellite for NavIC Augmentation

The Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) achieved another key space mission milestone with the successful orbital deployment of the NVS-03 satellite. The satellite is designed to strengthen and ensure the operational continuity of India's indigenous regional satellite navigation network, known as NavIC (Navigation with Indian Constellation).

### Key Mission Highlights & Operational Importance
* **System Enhancement:** The deployment of NVS-03 reinforces the satellite constellation responsible for delivering real-time positioning and timing services across the Indian mainland and adjacent regional areas.
* **Next-Generation Capabilities:** NVS-03 belongs to the second-generation series of navigation satellites (NVS) developed to expand regional coverage, improve user position accuracy, and support both civilian and strategic applications.
* **Boosting Technological Autonomy:** The continuous deployment of NVS series satellites underpins India's initiative to maintain independent regional positioning capabilities without relying exclusively on global satellite systems like GPS.
bullet_points: ISRO successfully launched the NVS-03 navigation satellite into orbit.
The mission enhances the operational capacity and signal continuity of the NavIC constellation.
NVS-03 is part of the second-generation navigation satellite series developed by ISRO.
NavIC provides accurate positioning and timing services over India and surrounding regions.
The satellite mission supports both civilian commercial applications and national strategic requirements.
The successful launch reflects ongoing national efforts to strengthen independent satellite navigation infrastructure.
key_facts: NVS-03 is a second-generation navigation satellite launched by ISRO.
NavIC stands for Navigation with Indian Constellation.
The launch aims to maintain continuity and enhance coverage of regional positioning services.
important_dates: October 31, 2026: ISRO successfully deployed the NVS-03 satellite.
exam_relevance: Prelims: Knowledge of ISRO's NVS series, NavIC coverage area, and regional satellite navigation architecture.
Mains: GS Paper 3 (Science & Technology) - India's space program, satellite navigation infrastructure, and self-reliance in strategic technologies.
news.upsc_analysis: The successful deployment of NVS-03 marks a crucial step in ensuring the operational longevity and precision of India's NavIC network. Robust regional navigation reduces dependency on foreign GPS networks, thereby safeguarding critical infrastructure, aviation, maritime transit, and national security capabilities.
causes: Need to reinforce and update the existing constellation of India's indigenous NavIC navigation system.
impacts: Enhances regional navigation coverage and positioning accuracy across India.
Strengthens strategic self-reliance in space-based positioning, navigation, and timing (PNT) services.
government_steps: Development and deployment of the next-generation NVS satellite series by ISRO under the Department of Space.
way_forward: Ensure timely launches of remaining NVS series satellites to maintain continuous, high-precision positioning services across all operational domains.
news.mains_notes:
### NavIC and NVS Satellite Series
- **Purpose:** Provide independent real-time positioning and timing services over India and a 1,500 km extended boundary.
- **NVS Series Role:** Next-generation satellite series designed to replace older IRNSS satellites, introducing upgraded atomic clocks and enhanced signal capabilities for both public and defense sectors.

Discuss the role of indigenous space infrastructure in securing critical services like defense, aviation, and disaster management in India.
news.takeaway: ISRO's successful launch of NVS-03 strengthens the NavIC network, boosting India's independent regional positioning and navigation capabilities.
prelims_facts: NVS-03 is a navigation satellite launched by ISRO to bolster the NavIC network.
NavIC stands for Navigation with Indian Constellation, delivering positioning services over India and surrounding regions up to 1,500 km.

### इसरो ने नाविक (NavIC) विस्तार के लिए NVS-03 उपग्रह का किया सफल प्रक्षेपण

- **Macroeconomic Significance:** The assessment highlights how technology-driven capital expenditure is increasingly influencing medium-term global economic trends.
- **Central Bank Perspective:** Tracking world economic growth projections remains vital for the RBI to gauge international demand trends, financial market movements, and prospective spillover effects on India's macroeconomic environment.
